bio:
Kossi Houngbedji is an award-winning sales leader with more than a decade of experience driving growth through strategic account management, negotiations, and business development across healthcare (medical technology & pharmaceuticals), software, and banking. Currently serving as an Academic Account Manager at GE HealthCare, Kossi partners with some of the nation’s leading healthcare organizations, helping deliver innovative solutions that improve patient care. He is an equipment Sales Advisory Board member and mentor.

Kossi will pursue his Executive MBA in Healthcare Leadership at the University of Tennessee’s Haslam College of Business.

bio: Dianna Jones is a Compliance Executive and Board Leader with over 20 years of experience helping organizations navigate complex regulatory, ethical, and commercial challenges across the technology and energy sectors. At Uber Technologies, she serves as Legal Director of Commercial & Emerging Risks, translating risk into strategy by driving risk-informed decisions across autonomous vehicle ecosystems, B2B partnerships, and commercial transactions, including M&A, while partnering with business and product leaders.

bio: Krystal Denley Bowen is Vice President and Chief Privacy Officer at Uber Technologies, Inc., where she leads the global privacy and cybersecurity legal teams and Co-Chairs Uber’s AI Law & Ethics Council. A veteran leader at the intersection of privacy, AI, and cybersecurity, Krystal brings decades of experience enabling organizations to innovate responsibly while maintaining customer trust and navigating the evolving global regulatory landscape.

name: Kweli Zukeri
title: Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation and Strategy
brief: Dr. Kweli Zukeri is Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation & Strategy at Howard University, where he has served for over 15 years.
bio:
Dr. Kweli Zukeri is Assistant Vice President of Web Innovation & Strategy at Howard University, where he has served for over 15 years. He led the development of a centralized web system supporting more than 90 University sites and now advances Howard’s adoption of AI-powered technologies.

A founding member of Howard’s Presidential AI Council, he helps shape responsible AI strategy and governance. His research explores technology, identity, psychological development, and social justice, with a current focus on protecting youth engagement with generative AI while strengthening critical thinking and critical AI literacy.

name: Kyle Leverett

bio: Kyle Leverett is a strategic content operations, programming, and talent partnerships leader with 13+ years of experience across production, content strategy, editorial programming, and creator ecosystems. At Snap Inc., he focuses on building and scaling strategic relationships with top creators, talent agencies, and entertainment partners. He has worked on shows like Glee, How To Get Away With Murder, Scandal, Black-ish and Family Guy. Kyle plays basketball and pickleball in his spare time and is an avid movie watcher.

name: Kyle McBrien

bio: Kyle McBrien is a Senior Financial Planner at Betterment, where he provides personalized financial advice and focuses on savings strategies to help clients achieve their financial goals. Previously, he worked at a large Chicago RIA serving high-net-worth clients with investment management, tax optimization, and wealth-transfer strategies. Kyle has been featured in The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Fortune, and MarketWatch. He graduated from Indiana University with a degree in finance and lives in Chicago.

name: Lamarr Henry

bio: Lamarr Henry is a security engineer at Figma and a lecturer at The Ohio State University, where he teaches the next generation to build and break complex systems. With a Master’s in Cybersecurity from Georgia Tech and a background in reverse engineering at Battelle, he has spent his career at the intersection of offensive and defensive security. From architecting serverless cloud environments to scaling secure infrastructure at P&G, Lamarr focuses on building security into the foundation of products. He is driven by the belief that true technical mastery comes from understanding how to dismantle a system as well as you assemble it.

name: LaRico Treadwell
title: CEO
brief: LaRico Treadwell, Ph.D., is a chemist and materials scientist with 10+ years in government and scientific research.
bio: LaRico Treadwell, Ph.D., is a chemist and materials scientist with 10+ years in government and scientific research. He holds a B.S. in Chemistry from the University of Mississippi and a Ph.D. in Inorganic/Solid State Chemistry from LSU. His expertise spans nanomaterials, composites, 3D printed corrosion sensors, radiation sensors, and autonomous smart devices, with 40+ publications and 15+ patents. As CEO of E4 Power, he partners with HBCUs, universities, and nonprofits on STEM workforce development, grant management, and tech transfer, helping secure and pursue over $400M in grant funding and leading 50+ professional workshops.

name: Larry Jones
title: CEO
brief: Larry Jones is one of the most recognizable and trusted voices in the stock market and cryptocurrency education space.
bio: Larry Jones is one of the most recognizable and trusted voices in the stock market and cryptocurrency education space. Since launching his financial education platform in 2020, he has helped hundreds of thousands of individuals gain confidence in investing, wealth building, and financial literacy. Through his YouTube channel, educational programs, live events, and speaking engagements, he has made investing accessible to everyday people seeking to create generational wealth and financial independence. His content focuses on stocks, cryptocurrency, options, market trends, portfolio management, and practical wealth-building strategies.

name: Larry Quinlan
title: Fortune 500 & Private Equity Company Board Director
company: Former Global Chief Information Officer, Deloitte
brief: Larry Quinlan has over 35 years of experience creating value through inspired, strategic leadership.
bio:
Larry Quinlan has over 35 years of experience creating value through inspired, strategic leadership. He is a digital and technology transformation expert with extensive experience in complex enterprise systems integrations, cybersecurity, technology organizational design, and global shared services models. He is sought after for his understanding of the strategic impacts of emerging technologies including analytics, AI, cloud and mobility. Larry most recently served as Global Chief Information Officer for

Deloitte, the $50B professional services firm. He had responsibility for all facets of technology strategy and operations, leading over 10,000 IT professionals in 175 countries. He led Deloitte’s global implementations of ERP systems, including some of the world’s largest SAP and Salesforce platforms leveraging data analytics, cloud, and collaboration technologies from AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, and ServiceNow. He also led the development of proprietary, custom technology platforms critical to Deloitte’s profitability. Larry and his team successfully executed post-merger technology integration for Deloitte’s acquisitions. He worked directly with the firm’s Global Board as leader of a multi-billion-dollar global technology and cyber program.

In addition to his CIO role, Larry drove significant revenue delivering services to Deloitte global clients in the hospitality and technology sectors. He advised company boards and CEOs on a range of IT, cyber, and digital strategic priorities. Larry led the Deloitte CIO Academy, a leadership development program for client executives aspiring to the corporate CIO role.

Larry serves on the Boards of three Fortune 500 companies: ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW), a cloud digital workflow leader, where he sits on the Audit Committee; Jones Lang LaSalle (NYSE: JLL), a global leader in real estate where chairs the Audit & Risk Committee while serving on the Nominating, Governance & Sustainability Committees; and Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), the leading provider of online travel, where he chairs the Board’s Cyber Subcommittee. Larry is also Board Director of UBS Americas where he chairs the Technology & Cyber Committee. He is Chairman of the Board at Hexaware Technologies and serves on and advises other private equity portfolio company boards. Larry is active in non-profit governance…he chairs the NPower Emeritus Board and the Technology Committee of United Way of Miami. He is a past Board co-chair of Global Leadership Forum and a former Board member of the Executive Leadership Council (ELC). Larry is NACD Directorship Certified and serves on the NACD 2024 Blue Ribbon Commission on Board Oversight of Technology.

Larry is a founding member of The TechPACT, a CIO organization committed to bridging the digital divide. He mentors startups at The Venture Mentoring Team. Larry is an avid boater and diver. He holds an MBA from Baruch College, CUNY and a BSc (Hons) from the University of the West Indies. In 2018, he was inducted into the CIO Hall of Fame and The University of the West Indies conferred an Honorary Doctor of Laws (LLD) degree in recognition of his leadership in industry.

name: Lawrence Miller
title: Deputy Program Manager for Acquisitions and Procurement Oversight,

bio: Lawrence L. Miller is Deputy Program Manager for Acquisitions and Procurement Oversight for NASA's Space Communications and Navigation (SCaN) Program, overseeing a multi-billion-dollar portfolio of 84 contracts across NASA's deep space, near space, and relay networks. He previously served as Director of Contracts for NASA's Office of JPL Management and Oversight and Deputy Director of NASA's Enterprise Pricing Office. He holds a B.S. in Finance from Southern University and an M.S. in Management Information Systems from Texas Southern University, and is a recipient of the NASA Silver Achievement Medal.

name: Leah Anise
title: Creator Partnerships, Consumer and Growth
brief: Leah Seay Anise leads Creator Partnerships across OpenAI’s Consumer and Growth verticals in the U.S. and Canada, helping influential creators explore and use AI.
bio: Leah Seay Anise leads Creator Partnerships across OpenAI’s Consumer and Growth verticals in the U.S. and Canada, helping influential creators explore and use AI. She built OpenAI’s creator marketing function from the ground up and previously led consumer communications for ChatGPT and Sora. Her career spans Uber, Amazon, and General Motors. A 2025 EBONY Power 100 honoree and New York Women in Communications Trailblazer, Leah serves on Delta Air Lines’ Technology Advisory Board and founded a scholarship supporting aspiring journalists, marketers, and communications professionals.

name: Lee Merritt
title: National Civil Rights Attorney & Community Organizer for Landmark Cases | Adjunct Professor at Harvard | Forbes Power 100 Attorney | Congressional Black Caucus Nation Builder | Top 10 Influential Leader |
brief: S. Lee Merritt is a nationally recognized civil rights attorney and Movement Lawyer who represents families in landmark cases including the killings of Ahmaud Arbery, Botham Jean, and Atatiana…
bio: S. Lee Merritt is a nationally recognized civil rights attorney and Movement Lawyer who represents families in landmark cases including the killings of Ahmaud Arbery, Botham Jean, and Atatiana Jefferson. Based in Texas with a federal practice rooted in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, he uses Section 1983 litigation, qualified immunity challenges, and federal oversight to hold institutions accountable when local systems fail. Merritt has used platforms before Congress and international bodies to testify on policing and human rights, extending the impact of his cases beyond individual verdicts.

name: Lindsay K. Smith
title: Director of Philanthropic Partnerships & Stewardship
brief: Lindsay Smith is Director of Philanthropic Partnerships and Stewardship for the Best Buy Foundation, where she leads strategic partnerships, stewardship, and mission-driven activations that help…
bio:
Lindsay Smith is Director of Philanthropic Partnerships and Stewardship for the Best Buy Foundation, where she leads strategic partnerships, stewardship, and mission-driven activations that help create pathways to tech-enabled careers and economic mobility for young people.

She brings more than 15 years of experience across philanthropy, higher education, and corporate social impact. Before joining Best Buy in 2025, Lindsay led strategic partnerships at Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business, advancing national and global initiatives focused on entrepreneurship, workforce development, financial capability, and social impact.

name: Lisa Glover-Gardin

bio: Lisa Glover Gardin is Vice President, Associate General Counsel, Privacy and Product and Chief Privacy Officer at Ancestry, where she leads legal strategy for privacy, regulatory compliance, and product innovation. Before Ancestry, she served as Global Head of Privacy Legal at PayPal, overseeing global privacy strategy and regulatory compliance. Lisa also held senior legal leadership roles at Google and Meta's Reality Labs, helping launch consumer products with privacy-by-design principles. She earned law degrees from Santa Clara University and UC Berkeley School of Law.

name: Loida Nicolas Lewis
title: Author
brief: Loida Nicolas Lewis is a distinguished businesswoman, philanthropist and author.
bio: Loida Nicolas Lewis is a distinguished businesswoman, philanthropist and author. After the untimely death of Reginald F. Lewis, the first African American to build a billion-dollar company, she led TLC Beatrice International as CEO and now continues his legacy as chair of The Reginald F. Lewis Foundation. Born in the Philippines, she became the first Asian woman to pass the New York State Bar Examination without attending a U.S. law school. She is a prominent advocate for immigrant rights, AANHPI representation, education, and Filipino-American civic engagement.

name: Lucas Isaza
title: Product Lead
brief: Lucas Isaza leads product for Buzz, Block’s open source workspace where people and AI agents build together.
bio: Lucas Isaza leads product for Buzz, Block’s open source workspace where people and AI agents build together. Before Buzz, Lucas built restaurant technology at Square and cofounded a commerce platform in Latin America that helped corner stores order inventory from consumer goods companies. He studied computer science and economics at Stanford University and brings a builder’s perspective to turning emerging technology into products people can use in their everyday work.

name: Marcello Farrell

brief: Marcello Farrell is a Sales Engineer at Descript, where he helps creators, marketers, and media teams fit the software to the actual work of making something worth listening to.
bio:
Marcello Farrell is a Sales Engineer at Descript, where he helps creators, marketers, and media teams fit the software to the actual work of making something worth listening to.

Outside Descript, Marcello is an Audio Engineer and gigging drummer with years under his belt in both. He spent years making visual work in the greater St. Louis glitch art scene, all while while drumming, managing, and recording local bands and artists across genres such as pop, rock, r&b, rap, and alternative.

name: Mary Robinson Carter

brief: Mary Robinson Carter is a First Vice President and Wealth Management Advisor who helps technology professionals, founders, and executives navigate the financial complexities of equity compensation…
bio:
Mary Robinson Carter is a First Vice President and Wealth Management Advisor who helps technology professionals, founders, and executives navigate the financial complexities of equity compensation, pre-IPO stock, stock options, RSUs, and liquidity events.

Recognized by Forbes as a Top Wealth Management Advisor and Top Wealth Management Team member in 2024, 2025, and 2026, Mary specializes in helping clients convert concentrated equity positions and career success into sustainable, long-term wealth strategies. She also serves on the CEO Advisory Council of the National Society of Black Engineers.

name: Melvin Hillsman
title: Principal Software Engineer
brief: Melvin Hillsman is a Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat who believes the most powerful technology is the kind people can not only use but build.
bio: Melvin Hillsman is a Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat who believes the most powerful technology is the kind people can not only use but build. He works at the intersection of AI, cloud-native infrastructure, and systems architecture — building bridges between what's possible and what's practical. Considering the power of storytelling — problems, constraints, and people — his talks are about the journey, showing how emerging and future tools collapse the distance between idea and working software. He is particularly driven to ensure that people aren't just invited to technological revolutions but equipped to build in them.

name: Michael A. Tinsley
title: Author
brief: Michael Tinsley is a debut author and a graduate of North Carolina A&T State University. He is a member of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated and currently resides in Bowie, Maryland.
bio: Michael Tinsley is a debut author and a graduate of North Carolina A&T State University. He is a member of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Incorporated and currently resides in Bowie, Maryland. Michael enjoys speaking with students at schools to promote literacy and volunteers across several initiatives in support of his community. Michael also enjoys independent coffee shops, all things X-Men related, and spending time with his family. May a Divine Awaken is his first novel in a new young adult fantasy series.

name: Michael Hawthorne Jr
title: Co-Founder
brief: Michael Hawthorne Jr. is Co-Founder of Klean Energy Kulture, CEO of Electric Kulture, and Head of Planning for Atlanta Climate Week.
bio: Michael Hawthorne Jr. is Co-Founder of Klean Energy Kulture, CEO of Electric Kulture, and Head of Planning for Atlanta Climate Week. An environmentalist, climate justice advocate, and cultural innovator, he bridges clean energy, entertainment, and community engagement to make climate action accessible and relevant. His career includes work with Greenpeace, the Sierra Club's Beyond Coal campaign, and national environmental initiatives. Through Klean Energy Kulture, Michael leverages music, storytelling, and pop culture to amplify underrepresented voices, accelerate clean energy adoption, and build a more inclusive climate economy.

name: Michael Penn, Jr., MD, PhD
title: Head of External Engagement, Population Health Center of Excellence
brief: Michael L. Penn, Jr., MD, PhD is Head of External Engagement for Genentech’s Population Health Center of Excellence, where he and his team drive strategies and cultivate partnerships that connect…
bio: Michael L. Penn, Jr., MD, PhD is Head of External Engagement for Genentech’s Population Health Center of Excellence, where he and his team drive strategies and cultivate partnerships that connect industry, healthcare stakeholders, lawmakers, and communities to define and advance the future of population health. A physician-scientist and nationally recognized leader in inclusive innovation, his work focuses on ensuring that breakthroughs in science and technology translate into meaningful improvements in health for all communities.

name: Michelle Grover
title: Enterprise Technology Executive & Board Member
brief: Michelle Grover is a visionary enterprise technology executive and board member with over 30 years of experience leading high-performing, global technology organizations.
bio: Michelle Grover is a visionary enterprise technology executive and board member with over 30 years of experience leading high-performing, global technology organizations. Most recently, she served as the first Chief Technology Officer at Slalom, where she oversaw the global technology organization which included infrastructure, data, enterprise IT and architecture. Renowned for her "Buy the Foundation, Build the Advantage" philosophy, Michelle has a proven track record of managing capital budgets up to $150M and decoupling revenue growth from operational overhead. Prior to her tenure at Slalom, she held leadership roles at Twilio, SAP Concur, and First Command. Michelle is recognized for driving innovation, scaling operations, and advising companies on emerging technology and growth strategy.

name: Michelle John

bio: Dr. Michelle John is a tenured professor of Biology and the inaugural Vice President for Research and Innovation at Texas Southern University, where she oversees 14 research centers and institutes. She leads the $40M Catalyst for Urban Transformation and launched the Institute for Urban Public Health & Housing. Under her leadership, TSU proposal submissions grew from $90M to over $156M, and external funding rose from $32M to over $54M. She is a PI on the $9.9M+ FORGE initiative and leads a $4.9M U.S. Department of Education grant. She chairs the USRA HBCU Science and Technology Council and holds a Ph.D. from Virginia Tech.

name: Michellene Davis

bio: Michellene Davis leads National Medical Fellowships, the country’s oldest health equity organization, working at what she calls the intersection of wealth and health. She was the first woman and first person of color to become Executive Vice President in RWJBarnabas Health’s 152-year history, and before that was the first African American to serve as New Jersey’s Acting State Treasurer, overseeing a $30 billion budget and a $70 billion pension portfolio.

name: Mike Jones

Mike Jones, VP of Security Platform Services for Nationwide, provides strategic direction and leadership for the Cyber Platform Services organization, leading our Identity & Access Management, Data Protection & Governance, Network, Platform, Endpoint and Cloud Security teams.

Mike has more than 20 years of experience in Information Technology roles and is well respected in the Tech industry having received various industry accolades. Mike served as the Nationwide Executive chair of IT Culture AAG and was selected to serve on the initial CEO associate advisory group. Corporate Connections awarded Mike the 2024 Man of the Year award.

name: Miles Braxton

bio: Miles Braxton is CEO and Co-Founder of Okovate, building the energy layer for the AI era through agrivoltaics: solar integrated with active farming. Okovate has secured over 180 MW in agrivoltaic development commitments and acquired Fundusol, an AI platform modeling crop and energy yield. Backed by the Schmidt Family Foundation, Okovate keeps farms in family hands. Miles previously held roles at Goldman Sachs Renewable Power and Summit Ridge Energy. A UVA graduate and Colorado Agrivoltaic Learning Center board member, he was named to Forbes 30 Under 30, EBONY Power 100, GreenBiz 30 Under 30, and AfroTech Future 50.

name: Millicent Auma

bio: Millicent is a GenAI Enablement Lead for Morgan Stanley’s Cyber Data Risk and Resilience division, focused on integrating AI across the business unit. She supports GenAI use case teams throughout the full lifecycle of their projects and works to identify synergies across departments, promoting common solutions for aligned business needs. With 5 years of experience in Technology, 2 focused on AI adoption, she specializes in bridging business and technology with hands on experience in Enterprise AI governance and strategy. She works closely with AI developers, compliance, and risk partners to ensure regulatory compliance across jurisdictions.

name: Monica Bowie
title: Product Marketing Director
brief: Monica Bowie carried the quota, and now she helps build how Salesforce sells AI.
bio: Monica Bowie carried the quota, and now she helps build how Salesforce sells AI. A Product Marketing Director with 15+ years of enterprise go-to-market leadership, she has driven $1B+ in pipeline and $300M+ in ACV while enabling 6,000+ sellers globally. She holds an MBA in Management of Technology from Georgia Tech. An avid runner and community wellness advocate, Monica founded The Tech Race, an annual 5K that brings runners and walkers in tech together.

name: Monica Melton

brief: Monica Melton is an Assistant Editor at New York Public Radio/WNYC.
bio: Monica Melton is an Assistant Editor at New York Public Radio/WNYC. bio: Simone Ashley Tyler is a dynamic media professional with over a decade of experience in media, community engagement, and platform building. bio: Stacey Abrams is a New York Times bestselling author, entrepreneur and political leader. bio: Steve Stoute is the Founder and CEO of UnitedMasters, a premium music technology platform empowering independent artists. bio: Symoné B. is a Principal Radar Systems Engineer with over 15 years of experience supporting mission-critical technology programs across defense, aerospace, and federal sectors. bio: Tamira Chapman is a trailblazing entrepreneur, philanthropist, and the founder of Storehouse In A Box, LLC (SIAB). Tanya Sam is an entrepreneur, angel investor, media personality, and co-founder of Elizabeth & Minnie Publishing, an independent publishing house amplifying underrepresented voices. name: Travis Cleaves
title: Deputy Director of Research Informatics and Data Science
company: American Society of Hematology Research Collaborative
brief: Travis Cleaves is the Deputy Director of Research Informatics and Data Science at the ASH Research Collaborative (ASH RC), the research arm of the American Society of Hematology — the world’s…
bio:
Travis Cleaves is the Deputy Director of Research Informatics and Data Science at the ASH Research Collaborative (ASH RC), the research arm of the American Society of Hematology — the world’s leading professional organization dedicated to the study and treatment of blood disorders. In this role, he leads initiatives in EHR data collection, quality assurance, and system optimization, driving the seamless integration of EHR and real-world data into ASH RC’s Data Hub to power hematologic disease research. His work is central to advancing clinical studies focused on Sickle Cell Disease and Multiple Myeloma.

With deep expertise in health information management and informatics, Travis has implemented EHR systems at scale, conducted interface testing and architecture reviews, and optimized clinical data workflows across platforms, including Cerner Millennium and Epic. He brings advanced technical fluency in HL7 v2, FHIR/JSON, and SQL, enabling robust EHR integration, interoperability, and regulatory compliance. Prior to joining ASH RC, he served as a Health Informatics Subject Matter Expert at Booz Allen Hamilton and as an Interface Architect and EHRM Ambulatory Portfolio Lead at MicroHealth, LLC, where he led cross-functional teams in EHR integration and Meaningful Use attestations.

Travis holds a BS in Biology from Prairie View A&M University and an AAS in Practical Nursing from Lone Star College. He is a Certified ScrumMaster® (CSM®) and holds an Information Privacy and Security (IPS) certification. His rare combination of clinical nursing background, systems architecture expertise, and research informatics leadership gives him a uniquely grounded perspective on the human stakes of the data decisions the health tech industry makes every day.

bio:
Vanessa Wyche is the director of NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, home to America’s astronaut corps, Mission Control Center, International Space Station, and Orion Programs. Her responsibilities included a broad range of human spaceflight activities, including development and operation of human spacecraft and NASA astronaut selection and training.

Wyche also oversees NASA Johnson’s activities supporting the commercialization of low Earth orbit, supporting the agency’s needs following the transition from the International Space Station in 2030, and led the center’s programs supporting the exploration of the Moon and Mars, including surface system capabilities for human and commercial robotic missions, as well as simulated missions for crews on Mars.

A PhD pursuant at the University of Rochester, her research explores cardiovascular disparities among Black women. Her work focuses on ensuring that nurses, Black communities, and underserved populations help shape the future of AI and healthcare.

bio: Vernessa Pollard is a Partner at DLA Piper and Chair of its FDA practice in Washington, D.C., advising life sciences, medical device, and technology companies on FDA regulatory and compliance matters. bio: Walter Powell Jr. is CEO of UnityCloud, a technology entrepreneur and former NFL player who has built ventures spanning civic technology and AI infrastructure. A three-time founder, Walter is focused on developing sustainable data centers in partnership with Tribal Nations, advancing energy sovereignty, data ownership, and economic opportunity. Through UnityCloud, he works to connect renewable energy, advanced computing, and community-centered development, creating pathways for Tribal communities to participate in and benefit from the infrastructure powering the AI economy.

name: Waverly Rose Brim
title: Research Engineer
brief: Waverly Rose Brim is an AI research engineer building intelligent systems at the intersection of computer vision, biological foundation models, and surgical data science.
bio:
Waverly Rose Brim is an AI research engineer building intelligent systems at the intersection of computer vision, biological foundation models, and surgical data science. Her work focuses on moving machine learning beyond the lab and into clinical environments where reliability, interpretability, and human decision-making matter.

She develops production-grade AI systems that transform patient records, imaging studies, pathology, and clinical guidelines into auditable, decision-ready intelligence for care teams. Her current projects include SCRUB, a surgical computer vision platform designed to track gloved hands in the operating room where conventional pose-estimation models break down; an optimized brain-to-image reconstruction framework capable of running on consumer hardware; and methods for evaluating the safety, fairness, and clinical risk of medical prediction algorithms.

Her earlier work spans multimodal computational pathology and genomics for meningioma characterization, AI-driven surgical skill assessment, operating room analytics, and DARPA-supported neural engineering efforts developing genetically encoded voltage indicators. She has authored more than 20 peer-reviewed publications in medical artificial intelligence and neuro-oncology and previously moderated the “Dr. AI” session at the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions in Tianjin, China.

Brim is currently pursuing an M.S. in Artificial Intelligence at Johns Hopkins University and is driven by a simple question: How do we build AI systems that clinicians can trust, patients can benefit from, and society can responsibly scale?

name: Wayne Dennis

bio: Wayne Dennis builds infrastructure-scale security organizations from nothing. He leads where security, infrastructure, and AI are the same problem. As CISO for Global OT Security at Solventum, he built the program from a blank page — securing the factories, labs, and connected devices behind patient care, where a breach is a safety event, not a data event. bio:

systems, and measures how those system reshape us. A software engineer by trade, X spent two decades building technology for Google, Microsoft, and public sector. bio: Yemi Akisanya has spent his 20+ year career answering one question: What does it take for people to do the best work of their lives? Today, as Vice President of Culture and People Experience at Axon, he leads a global strategy that ties belonging to high performance in service of a mission to protect life. He has transformed cultures on four continents, teaches MBA students, and serves on boards advancing economic opportunity. To thousands, he is proof that how we treat people is strategy. bio: Zekarias Amsalu is a fintech entrepreneur, ecosystem builder, and Co-Founder of the Africa Fintech Summit, a premier biannual gathering connecting leaders across Africa and global markets.
